records.name: First Presbyterian Church of Olney
records.summary: A Presbyterian congregation in Olney with Sunday worship, a weekly Wednesday Bible study, and a women's group that is collecting clothing and supplies for a foster family closet.
records.what_you_do: Join Sunday worship or the Wednesday Bible study, both at 11 am, take part in the women's circle groups or the men's Bible study, or donate to a drive. Youth and senior groups also meet through the church.

schedule.text: Sunday worship at 11 am year round, Sunday School for all ages at 10 am, and Wednesday Bible study at 11 am. In summer, worship moves to the air-conditioned chapel.

cost.text: No cost is listed for worship or activities. Giving is by donation.

first_step.how: Come to Sunday worship at 11 am, or call the church office (Wednesday to Friday, 12:40 to 6 pm) to ask about the Wednesday Bible study or a women's or men's group
first_step.basis: Worship is public with a clear time and office contact, and the activities page says you do not need to be a member and that all are welcome, but no page describes what a first visit is like
first_step.what_to_expect: Worship starts at 11 am on Sunday. A children's program for kindergarten to 5th grade runs during the sermon, and nursery care is offered during the service. The site does not say how long the service lasts or whether visitors are greeted, so the office is the best place to ask.
first_visit_tips: Call the office to ask about parking and wheelchair access, which the site does not describe
Sunday School for all ages meets at 10 am, before worship
Children can go to the nursery or to Children's Church during the service

records.notes: The home page says the chapel is used from the second Sunday of June through Labor Day, so the sanctuary applies in fall. The services page lists 11 am worship year round. The activities page names several groups but gives no costs and no years. The Presbyterian Women fall gathering is listed for a Saturday in October with no year, so it is not counted as evidence. The foster closet drive asks for new clothing, pajamas, hygiene items and toys, with no deadline given.

records.name: First Tee of Greater Philadelphia
records.summary: A golf program for young people in the Philadelphia area. It runs First Tee programs, girls' golf, a caddie academy, and Down the Shore programs, and it offers scholarships for participants.
records.what_you_do: Kids ages 5 to 18 join golf sessions that build golf skills and life skills, and can take part in girls golf and other programs. Adults can volunteer as coaches after a background check and SafeSport training.

schedule.text: Sessions run through the year. Each class lasts one hour. Session dates change, so check the registration page.

cost.text: A $20 yearly membership per child covers registration for any program during the year. Financial aid can be requested when you sign up.

requirements.gear: Water bottle, comfortable clothes and closed-toe shoes. Coaches and volunteers supply the golf equipment, and labeled personal clubs are welcome.

first_step.how: For kids: create an account on the Register page, buy the $20 yearly membership, and sign up for a session. For adult coaches: contact Jake Ruane, Program Manager, and fill out the information form.
first_step.basis: The FAQ says no experience is needed and walks through registration, and the volunteer page says all experience levels are welcome with training provided
first_step.what_to_expect: Each class lasts one hour and opens with a warm up, then moves into activities that build golf skills and life skills. Coaches and volunteers supply the equipment, so kids only need comfortable clothes and closed-toe shoes. Adult volunteers observe a class before they start coaching.
first_visit_tips: Bring a water bottle, comfortable clothes and closed-toe shoes
If you bring your own clubs, label them with first and last name
Watch for the confirmation email after you register, and a reminder the day before class

records.notes: Most session dates on the register page are printed without a year, so none are recorded. Class days and times are not stated. The locations page groups 31 locations by county and gives no addresses, so only the three Philadelphia locations are listed. The programs page does not describe the caddie academy, girls golf, Down the Shore or scholarship details, so those are named but not described. The newest dated item is a news story from Sept 25, 2026.

records.name: First United Methodist Church of Germantown
records.summary: A United Methodist congregation in Germantown that describes itself as a Reconciling Congregation, hosts a neighborhood meal with the Germantown Community Fridge, and holds a back to school drive.
records.what_you_do: Come to Sunday worship in person or online, join the Wednesday Bible study on Zoom, come to a Neighbor Table meal or the back to school drive, or ask about the women's and men's groups.

schedule.text: Sunday worship in the sanctuary and on YouTube, plus Adult Academy at 9:30 am on Sundays. Bible study meets Wednesdays at 1:30 pm on Zoom. The site lists Sunday worship at both 10 am and 11 am, so confirm the time by phone.

cost.text: No cost is listed for worship, Adult Academy or Bible study.

first_step.how: Visit Sunday worship in person or online, or send a note through the Connect With Us form on the church site
first_step.basis: The church says first-time visitors are warmly welcome at worship, and its Connect page gives a form and an office email for people who want to get connected
first_step.what_to_expect: Sunday worship is held in the sanctuary and streamed on YouTube. Adult Academy at 9:30 am is a Sunday class held in the parlor or on Zoom. The site does not describe what a first visit is like, how long worship runs, or where to park.
first_visit_tips: Call the office at 215-438-3677 to confirm the Sunday start time, since the site lists two
Watch the YouTube livestream first if you want a preview
The site does not say where to park or whether the building is wheelchair accessible, so ask when you call

records.notes: The home page banner says Sunday worship is at 11 am, while the Sunday services section says 10 am. A site search result also gave 10 am and mentioned Sunday classes during worship, but no page confirming that was read, so it is not used. Parking, wheelchair access and directions are not stated. The Bible study email link does not match the visible address (newsome vs wailoo), so no Bible study contact is recorded. Dated events on the site: Back to School Drive on Aug 16, 2026 (free), and a Neighbor Table meal on July 18, 2026. Some event listings omit the year and are not counted.

records.name: Fishtown Playschool
records.summary: A cooperatively run playschool in Fishtown where young children learn through play, using ideas from Reggio Emilia, emergent curriculum and Montessori.
records.what_you_do: Children attend a play-based class three mornings a week. Families apply online and pay a fee, and each family takes part in running the cooperative.

schedule.text: Classes meet Monday, Wednesday and Friday from 9 am to 12:30 pm. An extended day for pre-K children costs extra.

cost.text: A $30 application fee per family, plus a $250 membership fee for new families before enrollment. Tuition is not published. The extended day for pre-K costs extra.

first_step.how: Complete the online application and pay the $30 family fee through the link on the apply page. Applications are taken all year.
first_step.basis: A family must apply and pay a fee before the class list, and new families then pay a $250 membership fee. The pages disagree on whether tours are open before applying, so the way in is not clear
first_step.what_to_expect: Children aged two to five attend Monday, Wednesday and Friday mornings in two age groups, 2 to 3 and 3 to 5, each with a lead teacher. Each family commits to at least 20 hours a month, including classroom helper shifts, a committee, and All Hands meetings. Each child brings a packed lunch, and the school has no outdoor play area, so classes walk the neighborhood when the weather allows.
first_visit_tips: Pack a lunch your child can open alone, since the school asks for containers and packaging that kids can manage
Plan for classroom helper shifts several times a month, and a committee role for at least one parent
Potty training is not required
Email info@fishtownplayschool.org to ask whether a tour is open before you apply

records.notes: The apply page says tours open only after a family has applied and that applications are accepted all year. The FAQ page says prospective families can attend monthly tours and a classroom morning before enrollment. The pages disagree, so the first step follows the apply page and the tour question is left for the school to answer. Enrollment is first come, first served from a waitlist, with September as the main entry point. The contact page lists no phone number. No dated news was found. The registration link from tier 1 was not re-opened.

records.name: Fletcher Street Urban Riding Club
records.summary: A nonprofit riding club in North Philadelphia that teaches young people to ride and care for horses, with life skills and school support built in. Riding is free for kids and families.
records.what_you_do: Learn to ride, groom and care for horses, and take part in club life that centers on school and goals. Families can also sign up to volunteer.

schedule.text: Riding and stable work happen on a regular weekly schedule set by the club.

locations.label: Club address (contact page), Strawberry Mansion area

cost.text: Riding is free for kids and families, according to a 2025 news report. The club's own site lists no fees, only a donate button.

first_step.how: Send the member request form on the club's site, which asks for your child's birth date and grade. Email info@fsurc.com for membership questions.
first_step.basis: Families send a request and wait for the club to review it, and under-18 applicants also meet by video with a parent and board members. The page does not promise approval or describe a visit, so the way in is not clear
first_step.what_to_expect: The club reviews each request and says it follows up within about a week. Children under 18 meet by video with a parent or guardian and board members before membership is decided. The club does not treat verbal membership agreements as binding, so any agreement is put in writing.
first_visit_tips: Plan for a parent or guardian to come along while the application is pending, since minors may only be at the stables with one
Weekday hours are by appointment, and weekend hours are 8 am to 2 pm
Get any membership agreement in writing

records.notes: The member request form was read only and was not filled in or submitted. The contact page gives a street address that fits the Strawberry Mansion area from tier 1, but the page does not say it is the stable. No minimum rider age is stated on any page read. The club's site has no lessons, schedule or FAQ pages. The footer copyright year is not counted as evidence. The first step rating moved from 3 to 2 because the form leads to a review, under-18 applicants need a video meeting, and the page does not promise a visit.

records.name: FRAME/SEQUENCE
records.summary: A print magazine, published twice a year, that features emerging photographers, writers and artists from Philadelphia and greater Pennsylvania. Local artists can submit work for an issue.
records.what_you_do: Submit photos, writing or art for an issue, or buy a past issue in the shop.

schedule.text: Published twice a year as a print magazine, with an open call for each issue.

cost.text: New applicants pay a $25 submission fee, while previously featured artists and DVAA members pay nothing. Past issues cost $20 to $25 each in the shop, with local pickup available.

first_step.how: Start a submission on the submissions page before the issue 4 window closes on Nov 15, 2026
first_step.basis: The open call is public, has a clear deadline and form, and is open to any artist or writer, but acceptance is by review and the selection criteria are not stated
first_step.what_to_expect: Submissions go through an external online form, and photo or art work is limited to 5 to 10 images per edition. Accepted pieces earn a one-time cash payment plus a share of royalties, and artists keep ownership of their work. The site does not describe selection criteria or when decisions are made.
first_visit_tips: Read the issue theme on the submissions page before you choose work to send
Use JPEG or PNG files at 300 dpi if you can, since 240 dpi is the minimum accepted, each under 10 MB
Buy a past issue in the shop first to see the magazine, with local pickup available

records.notes: The site lists two submission windows: Sept 15 to Nov 15, 2026 for issue 4, and June 20 to July 18, 2025 for the first issue, both in the FAQ text on the submissions page. Only the 2026 window is used as current, since the site does not say which applies to a new call. The events page lists an Oct 7, 2026 photographer meetup at Bartram's Garden as free, but its description says this summer, so that date is not used as the newest evidence. The shop and footer show a 2025 copyright, which is not counted. Team: founder Lily Colman and collaborator Peter Wight. Fiscal sponsor CultureWorks.

records.name: Frankford Monthly Meeting
records.summary: A Quaker meeting in Frankford that worships on Sunday mornings at its meetinghouse, with Zoom worship available on request. The meeting says children are welcome and holds family worship on fifth Sundays, but a regional listing says children's programs are suspended.
records.what_you_do: Join Sunday worship at 10:30 am at the meetinghouse, or email the clerk for the Zoom link. On fifth Sundays, children stay with the adults for worship and themed activities. The monthly business meeting is held on third Sundays after worship.

schedule.text: Sunday worship at 10:30 am at the meetinghouse, with Zoom worship on request. Family worship is held on fifth Sundays.

access.notes: One page says the meetinghouse is wheelchair accessible, but a regional listing says wheelchair access is suspended. Ask before you come.

first_step.how: Come to Sunday worship at 10:30 am at the meetinghouse, or email the clerk for the Zoom link.
first_step.basis: Worship has a clear time, place and email contact, and the meeting says children are welcome, but no page describes a newcomer welcome or what a first visit is like
first_step.what_to_expect: Worship starts at 10:30 am on Sunday in the meetinghouse. The meeting's pages do not say whether worship is silent or spoken, or how long it lasts. If you bring children, check first whether the Sunday children's time is running, because a regional listing says it is suspended.
first_visit_tips: Email the clerk for the Zoom link if you would rather join online
Call or email ahead to check whether the children's time is running before you bring children
The directions page covers driving routes only, and parking is not described, so plan transit and parking on your own

records.notes: The sources disagree on current status. The meeting's own legacy pages list First Day School at 10:30 am, say children are welcome, and describe a wheelchair accessible meetinghouse. A regional listing says First Day School, childcare and wheelchair access are suspended since the pandemic, with no date given, and it names a different clerk from the meeting's own page. The calendar page lists no events. The FMM page gives a callback phone number of (215) 241-1146, which differs from the 267-279-9168 number carried over from tier 1 and kept here, so verify before relying on either. The nearest SEPTA stop is not named as nearest: the directions page mentions the Margaret-Orthodox elevated station only as a landmark on a driving route, so it is not listed. Verify the children's program before sending children.

notes: Batch had 7 groups, not 6, so all 7 were covered. 32 WebFetch calls and 1 WebSearch used (site-restricted to fumcog.org, to settle a conflicting worship time). No blocked pages and no rate limiting. Conflicts recorded in group notes: Germantown worship time (10 am vs 11 am), Fishtown tour availability, Frankford current status and phone number, FRAME/SEQUENCE submission window. Fletcher Street first_step rating moved from 3 to 2 after reading the member request form. Every summary and what-to-expect sentence was written here in our own words.
